title: Search Engine Dorking
description: Learn how to use advanced search operators to find specific information during OSINT investigations. Dorking helps reduce noise and discover hidden publicly available data.

sections.title: What is Dorking?
sections.description: Search engine dorking is the use of special search queries and operators in search engines like Google and Bing to find more specific information. Instead of getting thousands of unrelated results, dorking helps filter and refine searches to find relevant information.
topics: Used by researchers, security professionals, and OSINT investigators
Works on Google, Bing, and other search engines
Helps reduce search noise and find hidden public data
Discover related usernames, identities, and documents
sections.note: Always perform OSINT ethically and legally. Finding publicly available information does not mean you have permission to misuse it.

sections.title: Exact Match — Quotes " "
sections.description: Quotation marks force the search engine to find the exact phrase instead of individual words. This is one of the most important and first techniques used during information gathering.

commands.description: Search for this exact phrase. Search engine will not split or modify the query.
Search for an exact email address. Useful when search engines treat @ and . differently.
Search for an exact username across indexed pages.
Search multiple formatting variations of the same identity to get broader results.

sections.title: Narrowing Results — Minus Operator
sections.description: When you get too many irrelevant results (search noise), use the minus operator to exclude specific keywords from results.

commands.description: Search for Shaheen College but exclude all results containing the word Bider.
Search for a name but exclude results from Facebook and Instagram.
Search for a keyword but exclude all Wikipedia results.

sections.title: Site Operator
sections.description: The site operator restricts search results to a specific website. Instead of searching the entire internet, focus on one specific platform.
sections.note: No space between operator, colon, and keyword. Correct: site:github.com — Wrong: site: github.com

commands.description: Search only inside GitHub for this exact username.
Find LinkedIn profiles matching this name and keyword.
Site mapping — shows all pages from this domain indexed by the search engine. Reveals publicly accessible content.
Search for a username specifically on Reddit.

sections.title: Filetype Operator
sections.description: Search for specific downloadable file types. Organizations often publish documents containing valuable public information.

commands.description: Search for PowerPoint presentations related to Cisco.
Search for PDF documents related to OSINT.
Search for Word documents related to a company.
Combine filetype with site operator for more targeted results.

sections.title: InURL Operator
sections.description: Search for specific keywords that appear inside a website's URL. Useful for discovering specific types of indexed pages and understanding web structure.

commands.description: Find pages where the word 'login' appears in the URL.
Find pages where the word 'admin' appears in the URL.
Advanced: find FTP-related PDF files about OSINT. Excludes http/https URLs. The | symbol means OR.
Find WordPress directory paths inside a specific website.

sections.title: Intitle & Allintitle Operators
sections.description: These operators search based on the HTML title tag of web pages. Every webpage has a title tag that search engines use during indexing.

commands.description: Find pages where the title contains the exact phrase 'coding books'.
Find pages where ALL these words (coding, books, python) appear in the title.
Find login pages on a specific website by searching page titles.

sections.title: Index Of Dork
sections.description: One of the most powerful OSINT dorks. Used to discover publicly accessible directory listings on web servers. When a server has directory listing enabled and no index file, it exposes all files inside that directory.
sections.note: Finding an open directory does not give you permission to download or use those files for unauthorized purposes. Always act ethically.

commands.description: Find publicly accessible directory listings containing OSINT-related files.
Classic index of dork to find open directory listings.
Find open directories containing PDF files.
Check if a specific website has any open directory listings.

sections.title: Combining Operators
sections.description: The real power of dorking comes from combining multiple operators together. This creates highly targeted searches and significantly reduces irrelevant results.

commands.description: Find PDF files on GitHub related to a specific username.
Find a person on LinkedIn but exclude job listing pages.
Find open directories with PDFs on a specific site.
Search for an email address but exclude major social media platforms.

sections.title: Asterisk Wildcard Operator *
sections.description: The asterisk acts as a wildcard when you don't know the complete phrase you're searching for. It tells the search engine to match any word in that position.

commands.description: Search for a phrase where the middle word is unknown. Useful when you only remember part of a name or phrase.
Find pages containing variations like 'target social account', 'target bank account', etc.

sections.title: Range Operator ..
sections.description: Search within a numerical range. Useful when investigating dates, numbers, counts, or prices where you know the approximate range but not the exact value.
sections.note: Not every search engine interprets operators the same way. Always try multiple search engines — one may have indexed information another hasn't.

commands.description: Search for pages related to sentinel octopus with comment counts between 1 and 30.
Search for a keyword within a year range.

sections.title: Related Operator
sections.description: Discover websites that the search engine considers related to a specific domain. Useful for expanding research beyond a single website during investigations.
sections.note: Results depend on the search engine's own indexing. Treat results as investigation leads, not a complete list of connections.

commands.description: Find websites related to this domain according to the search engine.
Discover potentially related online resources for any target domain.

sections.title: Date Filtering & URL Injection
sections.description: Filter search results by date to find information from a specific time period. Time is often an important piece of the puzzle in OSINT investigations.
topics: Use Google Search Tools → Any time → Custom range
Filter by past hour, day, week, month, or year
Useful for investigating old events, news stories, or specific years
Significantly reduces search noise when time period is known

commands.description: Append to Google search URL to filter results between 2018 and 2020. Modify dates as needed.

sections.title: Custom Search Engine (CSE)
sections.description: Create a custom search engine that searches only specific websites you define. Extremely useful when you repeatedly investigate a particular set of platforms or sources.
topics: Go to Google Programmable Search Engine and create a new engine
Add target domains you want to search within
Create refinements: Social Media, News, Technical Docs, Public Databases
Use your CSE instead of regular Google for focused investigations

commands.description: CSE URL structure. cx = your engine ID, num = results count, filter=0 disables duplicate filtering.

sections.title: Contains & Linkdomain Operators
sections.description: Additional operators for finding file references and domain links. Support varies between search engines — always test and verify results.
sections.note: These operators may not work on all search engines. If one doesn't work, combine other operators to reach the same goal.

commands.description: Find pages on cisco.com that contain links or references to PowerPoint files.
Discover pages that contain links referencing this domain. Useful for reconnaissance.

sections.title: Archives & Historical OSINT
sections.description: Archived copies allow investigators to view information that has changed, disappeared, or been removed from the live internet. A webpage deleted today may still exist in an archive.
sections.note: Archives don't contain every webpage. Availability depends on whether the page was crawled and saved by the service.

tools.name: Wayback Machine (archive.org)
tools.description: Largest web archive. Contains billions of saved webpages going back decades.

tools.name: archive.today
tools.description: Save and view archived snapshots of webpages. Also accessible via archive.is.

commands.description: Search Wayback Machine for archived versions of a specific domain.
Search for publicly indexed OSINT-related pages on newspaper archive sites.

sections.title: Google Advanced Search & Patents
sections.description: Two powerful Google tools for OSINT — Advanced Search for beginners who don't want to memorize operators, and Google Patents for researching inventors, organizations, and technology history.

tools.name: Google Advanced Search
tools.description: Build complex search queries using a form interface. Specify exact phrases, exclusions, file types, date ranges, and more without memorizing operators.

tools.name: Google Patents
tools.description: Search patent records to investigate inventors, organizations, patent filings, and technology history. Useful for researching companies and individuals.

resources.name: Google Advanced Search
resources.description: Official Google advanced search page. Build complex queries without memorizing operators.

resources.name: Google Hacking Database (GHDB)
resources.description: Large collection of Google dorks maintained by Exploit-DB. Reference for advanced dork queries.

resources.name: Wayback Machine
resources.description: Web archive service. View historical snapshots of any webpage.

resources.name: Google Patents
resources.description: Search patent records for investigating inventors, organizations, and technology history.
